overview: This Senate resolution allows the Senate's Sergeant at Arms, the officer in charge of security and operations in the Senate, to hold a blood donation drive once every three months during the current two-year Congress (2025 to 2026). The Sergeant at Arms picks the date of each drive after consulting the Senate Rules and Administration Committee, and chooses a location and a partner blood donation organization with that committee's approval. Senators may suggest specific blood donation groups to partner with. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 27, 2025.
for: Supporters say regular drives on Senate grounds make it easy for staff and visitors to give blood and help keep supplies up for hospitals.
against: Critics say the resolution only covers internal Senate arrangements and does nothing to address blood shortages more broadly.
